sections.h2: Public (SNS) vs. private vs. online — which is right for you?

items.title: SNS (public system)
items.text: Built around residents with a registered family doctor. As a tourist, your realistic public access point is the emergency room (urgência) — appropriate for genuine emergencies, but expect long waits for non-urgent issues.

items.title: Private clinic or hospital
items.text: Fast and often English-friendly in Lisbon, Porto, the Algarve and other tourist areas, but can be costly without insurance, and you have to travel there.

items.title: Online consultation (Lon Clinic)
items.text: Best for common, non-emergency issues. A doctor registered with the Portuguese Medical Association sees you by video. If needed, the prescription is electronic and works at any pharmacy in Portugal. Consultations: English, Spanish, Portuguese. €39, shown before checkout.

sections.h2: Do you need travel insurance or an EHIC/GHIC card?
paragraphs: EU/EEA citizens with an EHIC (or a UK GHIC) can access public healthcare at resident rates for necessary care — this does not cover private or online consultations.
Non-EU visitors should have travel insurance. Lon Clinic can issue a receipt for reimbursement if your policy covers outpatient or telemedicine care.
For a quick, non-emergency issue, an online consultation is often simpler than navigating insurance paperwork for public care.

sections.h2: Finding an English-speaking doctor
paragraphs: Major hospitals in Lisbon, Porto and the Algarve generally have English-speaking staff. Smaller towns and rural areas are less reliable.

You do not have to guess with Lon Clinic: say English, Spanish or Portuguese when you book. We do not currently offer French or German consultations — English covers most visitors who need one of those.

faq.q: Can a tourist just walk into a Portuguese hospital?
faq.a: Yes, for emergencies — public hospital emergency rooms treat everyone regardless of nationality. Non-residents may be billed, and it is not designed for minor issues.

faq.q: Is there a cost for using SNS as a tourist?
faq.a: Non-residents without an EHIC/GHIC or Portuguese registration are generally charged for care, including emergency visits.

faq.q: How quickly can I get an online consultation?
faq.a: Same-day appointments are often available, seven days a week. You choose the slot when you book. The consultation is €39.

faq.q: Will the prescription work at any pharmacy?
faq.a: When a prescription is issued, it is a Portuguese electronic prescription. You can collect it at any pharmacy in the country with the code sent by SMS or email.

sections.h2: Tips for your stay in Lisbon
paragraphs: Lisbon's steep hills and polished limestone pavements (calçada) cause a surprising number of sprained ankles and falls, especially when wet. Wear shoes with grip.
In summer, heat and long walking days lead to dehydration and heat exhaustion, and stomach upsets are among the most common reasons visitors look for a doctor.

sections.h2: Insurance and costs
paragraphs: Visitors from the EU, EEA and Switzerland can use the public health system with a European Health Insurance Card (EHIC). UK visitors can use a GHIC. That covers necessary public care. It does not pay for a private online consultation.
Everyone else should rely on travel insurance. Online consultations are paid directly. Keep the invoice and medical report to claim reimbursement, and check your policy's conditions first.

faq.q: Can a doctor in Portugal see me online and prescribe medication?
faq.a: Yes. After a video consultation, the doctor can prescribe what you need if it is clinically appropriate. The prescription is electronic and works at Portuguese pharmacies.

faq.q: Do I need a Portuguese health number?
faq.a: No. You can book with your passport or ID.

faq.q: When should I go to the hospital instead?
faq.a: For chest pain, trouble breathing, stroke signs, severe bleeding, a serious injury, loss of consciousness or a severe allergic reaction, call 112. Also go in person if the doctor tells you that you need an examination.

items.title: Clinique ou hôpital privé

sections.h2: Avez-vous besoin d’une assurance voyage ou d’une carte européenne d’assurance maladie ?
paragraphs: Les citoyens UE/EEE munis d’une CEAM (ou GHIC pour les Britanniques) peuvent accéder au système public au tarif résident pour les soins nécessaires — cela ne couvre pas les consultations privées ou en ligne.
Les visiteurs hors UE devraient avoir une assurance voyage. Lon Clinic peut émettre un reçu pour remboursement si la police couvre une consultation ambulatoire ou la télémédecine.
Pour un problème rapide et non urgent, une téléconsultation est souvent plus simple que la paperasse d’assurance pour les soins publics.

sections.h2: Trouver un médecin qui parle votre langue
paragraphs: Les grands hôpitaux de Lisbonne, Porto et de l’Algarve ont généralement du personnel anglophone. C’est moins fiable dans les petites villes et zones rurales.

Chez Lon Clinic, vous choisissez anglais, espagnol ou portugais à la réservation. Pas de consultation en français pour le moment : l’anglais ou l’espagnol couvrent la plupart des voyageurs francophones.

faq.q: Un touriste peut-il simplement se rendre dans un hôpital portugais ?
faq.a: Oui, en cas d’urgence — les urgences des hôpitaux publics soignent tout le monde quelle que soit la nationalité. Les non-résidents peuvent être facturés, et ce n’est pas prévu pour les problèmes mineurs.

faq.q: Utiliser le SNS en tant que touriste a-t-il un coût ?
faq.a: Les non-résidents sans CEAM/GHIC ni inscription portugaise sont généralement facturés pour les soins, y compris les visites aux urgences.

sections.h2: Can a Portuguese pharmacy help without a prescription?
paragraphs: Portuguese pharmacies (farmácias) are well trained. They can advise on pain relief and over-the-counter options for mild symptoms.
They cannot prescribe antibiotics. In Portugal a UTI antibiotic always needs a doctor. If symptoms are mild, the pharmacist is still a good first stop for what to do next.

faq.q: Can I buy UTI antibiotics over the counter in Portugal?
faq.a: No. Antibiotics require a prescription, even for a common UTI. A pharmacist can help with pain relief and next steps, not with an antibiotic on their own.

faq.q: How much does an online consultation cost?
faq.a: At Lon Clinic it is €39 for a video consultation. The prescription, if the doctor issues one, is included — no extra prescribing fee at checkout.

faq.q: Will the prescription work at any pharmacy?
faq.a: Yes. A Portuguese electronic prescription can be collected at any pharmacy in the country with the code sent by SMS or email.

faq.q: I am a man with these symptoms. Can I still book online?
faq.a: UTI in men is not treated as a simple cystitis. Do not use this page as a shortcut to antibiotics. If there is fever or loin pain, go to the ER. Otherwise book a general consultation and expect a more careful work-up, often in person.

sections.h2: What to do in the first 24 hours

items.title: Fluids first
items.text: Oral rehydration salts (sachets dissolved in water) replace salt and sugar better than water alone. Sip little and often. Clear soup and diluted juice also help; avoid alcohol.

items.title: Eat when you can
items.text: No need to fast. Plain food — rice, bread, bananas, soup — as soon as you feel like it.

items.title: Wash your hands
items.text: Soap and water after the toilet and before food. Stomach bugs spread quickly in shared holiday accommodation.

sections.h2: What Portuguese pharmacies sell without a prescription
paragraphs: Oral rehydration salts, paracetamol and — for adults without fever or blood in the stool — loperamide to reduce the number of trips to the toilet. The pharmacist will ask a few questions; mention other medicines and any pregnancy.
Antibiotics and stronger anti-sickness medicines need a prescription in Portugal. Most traveller’s diarrhoea does not need an antibiotic at all — a doctor decides when it does.

sections.h2: Food poisoning, a virus, or something else?
paragraphs: In the first days it makes little difference: fluids, rest, and watching for red flags. Norovirus spreads from person to person and often starts with sudden vomiting; bacterial food poisoning usually follows a specific meal by a few hours to a couple of days.
Diarrhoea lasting more than a week, or coming back after you get home, needs a proper assessment — sometimes with a stool test.

rows: Not improving after 48 h, need a plan, prescription or note
Red flags: blood, dehydration, severe pain

faq.q: Do I need antibiotics for traveller’s diarrhoea?
faq.a: Usually not. Most cases settle on their own with fluids. A doctor may prescribe an antibiotic for severe cases — for example high fever or many episodes a day — after assessing you.

faq.q: Can I take loperamide (Imodium)?
faq.a: Adults without fever and without blood in the stool can usually take it for a short time. Do not use it for children, or if there is blood, high fever or severe abdominal pain. Ask the pharmacist.

faq.q: Can I get a medical note for my travel insurance?
faq.a: If you had to cancel a flight or excursion, the doctor can issue a medical certificate after the video consultation when it is clinically justified. See our guide on doctor’s notes for travel insurance.

faq.q: Is tap water safe in Portugal?
faq.a: Yes. Tap water in Portugal is treated and generally safe to drink. Holiday stomach bugs usually come from food, other people or swimming water — not from the tap.

sections.h2: Why the pharmacy says no
paragraphs: Antibiotics are prescription-only medicines in Portugal. Pharmacists apply this strictly, including for visitors who bring an empty box.

A prescription from another EU country can in principle be dispensed in Portugal if it contains the required details, but many pharmacies are cautious with foreign paper prescriptions, and prescriptions from outside the EU are not accepted. A Portuguese electronic prescription avoids the problem.

items.title: Often needed
items.text: Uncomplicated cystitis in women, some skin infections, and some cases of tonsillitis or sinusitis that are not improving.

items.title: Usually not needed
items.text: Colds, flu, COVID, most sore throats and coughs, and most traveller’s diarrhoea. These are viral or settle on their own — an antibiotic adds side effects without speeding recovery.

items.title: Needs a dentist
items.text: Toothache and dental abscess need a dentist. An antibiotic alone does not fix the tooth.

faq.q: Will the doctor prescribe an antibiotic if I ask for one?

faq.q: Is my prescription from home valid in Portugal?
faq.a: EU prescriptions can in principle be dispensed if they contain the required details; non-EU prescriptions are not valid. If the pharmacy refuses, a video consultation can issue a Portuguese electronic prescription when appropriate.

sections.h2: Weever fish (peixe-aranha) — common on Portuguese beaches
paragraphs: The weever fish hides in the sand in shallow water, especially in the Algarve and on the west coast. Stepping on it causes sudden, intense pain in the foot.

First aid: soak the foot in water as hot as you can tolerate without scalding (test it with your other hand) for 30 to 90 minutes. Lifeguards know the drill. Paracetamol or ibuprofen helps. If the wound turns red, hot and swollen over the next days, see a doctor.
Beach shoes in shallow water, especially at low tide, prevent most stings.

sections.h2: Jellyfish and the Portuguese man o’ war (caravela-portuguesa)
paragraphs: Get out of the water. Rinse with seawater — not fresh water — and lift off any visible tentacles with tweezers or a gloved hand, without rubbing. Warm water can ease the pain afterwards.
Man o’ war stings are more painful and can cause general symptoms. Follow the lifeguards and the beach flags; if there is chest pain, difficulty breathing or collapse, call 112.

sections.h2: Sunburn and sun rash

items.title: Cool, not cold
items.text: Cool showers or damp cloths, plenty to drink, and after-sun or a light moisturiser.

items.text: Paracetamol or ibuprofen from the pharmacy, if you can normally take them.

items.title: Leave blisters alone
items.text: Do not pop them. Cover broken blisters with a clean dressing and stay out of the sun.

items.title: Sun rash
items.text: An itchy, bumpy rash on sun-exposed skin in the first days of a holiday is often polymorphic light eruption. Shade and an antihistamine from the pharmacy usually help; severe or persistent cases can be assessed on video.

sections.h2: Mosquitoes and ticks
paragraphs: Mosquito bites in Portugal are usually just itchy: an antihistamine tablet or cream from the pharmacy, and try not to scratch. Madeira has Aedes mosquitoes — use repellent there.

Remove ticks with fine tweezers close to the skin and note the date. Fever, headache or a rash in the following two weeks needs a doctor: Mediterranean spotted fever occurs in Portugal and is treatable.

faq.q: Can a doctor assess a rash on video?

faq.q: Can I get treatment for an infected bite?
faq.a: If the doctor diagnoses a bacterial skin infection, they can prescribe treatment by electronic prescription. Many red bites are just inflammation and do not need an antibiotic.

faq.q: What should I ask for at the pharmacy?
faq.a: For sunburn: after-sun or a soothing gel, and pain relief. For itchy bites: an oral antihistamine or a mild cream. Tell the pharmacist about other medicines and pregnancy.

sections.h2: Intoxication, virus ou autre chose ?
paragraphs: Les premiers jours, cela change peu : boire, se reposer, surveiller les signes d’alerte. Le norovirus se transmet de personne à personne et commence souvent par des vomissements brutaux ; l’intoxication bactérienne suit en général un repas précis, de quelques heures à deux jours après.
Une diarrhée qui dure plus d’une semaine, ou qui revient au retour, mérite une vraie évaluation — parfois avec une analyse de selles.

sections.h2: La vive (peixe-aranha) — fréquente sur les plages portugaises
paragraphs: La vive s’enfouit dans le sable en eau peu profonde, notamment en Algarve et sur la côte ouest. Marcher dessus provoque une douleur brutale et intense au pied.

Premiers secours : plongez le pied dans une eau aussi chaude que supportable sans vous brûler (testez avec l’autre main) pendant 30 à 90 minutes. Les sauveteurs connaissent le geste. Paracétamol ou ibuprofène soulagent. Si la plaie devient rouge, chaude et gonflée les jours suivants, consultez.
Des chaussures de plage dans l’eau peu profonde, surtout à marée basse, évitent la plupart des piqûres.

sections.h2: Méduses et galère portugaise (caravela-portuguesa)
paragraphs: Sortez de l’eau. Rincez à l’eau de mer — pas à l’eau douce — et retirez les filaments visibles avec une pince ou une main gantée, sans frotter. De l’eau chaude peut ensuite calmer la douleur.

La piqûre de galère portugaise est plus douloureuse et peut donner des symptômes généraux. Suivez les sauveteurs et les drapeaux de la plage ; en cas de douleur thoracique, de gêne respiratoire ou de malaise, appelez le 112.

sections.h2: Coup de soleil et lucite

items.title: Frais, pas froid
items.text: Douches fraîches ou linges humides, beaucoup d’eau à boire, et après-soleil ou crème hydratante légère.

items.title: Contre la douleur
items.text: Paracétamol ou ibuprofène en pharmacie, si vous les prenez habituellement sans problème.

items.title: Ne percez pas les cloques
items.text: Couvrez les cloques ouvertes d’un pansement propre et restez à l’ombre.

items.title: Lucite
items.text: Une éruption qui démange, en petits boutons, sur la peau exposée dans les premiers jours de vacances est souvent une lucite polymorphe. L’ombre et un antihistaminique de pharmacie aident en général ; les formes intenses ou persistantes peuvent être évaluées en visio.

sections.h2: Moustiques et tiques
paragraphs: Au Portugal, les piqûres de moustique ne font en général que démanger : un antihistaminique en comprimé ou en crème, et évitez de gratter. Madère compte des moustiques Aedes — utilisez un répulsif.

Retirez les tiques avec une pince fine, au ras de la peau, et notez la date. Fièvre, maux de tête ou éruption dans les deux semaines suivantes : consultez. La fièvre boutonneuse méditerranéenne existe au Portugal et se soigne.

faq.q: Un médecin peut-il évaluer une éruption en visio ?
faq.a: Souvent, oui — avec une bonne lumière et un gros plan. Si un examen en personne ou des analyses sont nécessaires, le médecin vous le dira.

faq.q: Peut-on traiter une piqûre infectée ?
faq.a: Si le médecin diagnostique une infection bactérienne de la peau, il peut prescrire un traitement par ordonnance électronique. Beaucoup de piqûres rouges ne sont qu’une inflammation et ne nécessitent pas d’antibiotique.

faq.q: Que demander à la pharmacie ?
faq.a: Pour un coup de soleil : après-soleil ou gel apaisant, et un antalgique. Pour des piqûres qui démangent : un antihistaminique oral ou une crème douce. Signalez vos autres traitements et une éventuelle grossesse.

faq.q: Combien ça coûte ?
faq.a: 39 € la téléconsultation. L’ordonnance, si elle est émise, est incluse.

sections.h2: Qué hacer en las primeras 24 horas

items.title: Primero, líquidos
items.text: Las sales de rehidratación oral (sobres disueltos en agua) reponen sal y azúcar mejor que el agua sola. Beba poco y a menudo. El caldo y el zumo diluido también ayudan; evite el alcohol.

items.title: Coma cuando pueda
items.text: No hace falta ayunar. Comida sencilla — arroz, pan, plátano, sopa — en cuanto le apetezca.

items.title: Lávese las manos
items.text: Agua y jabón después del baño y antes de comer. Los virus intestinales se contagian rápido en alojamientos compartidos.

sections.h2: Qué venden las farmacias portuguesas sin receta
paragraphs: Sales de rehidratación oral, paracetamol y — en adultos sin fiebre ni sangre en las heces — loperamida para reducir las deposiciones. El farmacéutico hará algunas preguntas; mencione otros medicamentos y un posible embarazo.
Los antibióticos y los antieméticos más potentes necesitan receta en Portugal. La mayoría de las diarreas del viajero no necesitan antibiótico — lo decide un médico.

sections.h2: ¿Intoxicación, virus u otra cosa?
paragraphs: En los primeros días apenas cambia nada: líquidos, reposo y vigilar las señales de alarma. El norovirus se contagia de persona a persona y suele empezar con vómitos bruscos; la intoxicación bacteriana suele aparecer entre unas horas y un par de días después de una comida concreta.
Una diarrea de más de una semana, o que vuelve al regresar a casa, necesita una valoración adecuada — a veces con análisis de heces.

faq.q: ¿Necesito antibiótico para la diarrea del viajero?
faq.a: Normalmente no. La mayoría se cura sola con líquidos. El médico puede recetar un antibiótico en casos graves — por ejemplo con fiebre alta o muchas deposiciones al día — tras valorarle.

faq.q: ¿Puedo tomar loperamida (Fortasec)?
faq.a: Los adultos sin fiebre y sin sangre en las heces suelen poder tomarla durante poco tiempo. No la use en niños, ni si hay sangre, fiebre alta o dolor abdominal intenso. Pregunte en la farmacia.

faq.q: ¿Me pueden hacer un informe para el seguro de viaje?
faq.a: Si tuvo que cancelar un vuelo o una excursión, la médica puede emitir un certificado tras la videoconsulta cuando esté clínicamente justificado. Vea nuestra guía sobre el certificado médico para el seguro de viaje.

faq.q: ¿Se puede beber el agua del grifo en Portugal?
faq.a: Sí. El agua del grifo en Portugal está tratada y en general es segura. Los problemas de estómago en vacaciones suelen venir de la comida, de otras personas o del agua de baño — no del grifo.

paragraphs: En Portugal los antibióticos son medicamentos sujetos a receta. Los farmacéuticos lo cumplen de forma estricta, también con turistas que traen la caja vacía.

Una receta de otro país de la UE puede, en principio, dispensarse en Portugal si tiene los datos exigidos, pero muchas farmacias son prudentes con recetas extranjeras en papel, y las de fuera de la UE no se aceptan. Una receta electrónica portuguesa evita el problema.

sections.h2: Cuándo sirve un antibiótico — y cuándo no

items.title: A menudo necesario
items.text: Cistitis no complicada en mujeres, algunas infecciones de piel y algunos casos de amigdalitis o sinusitis que no mejoran.

items.title: Normalmente innecesario

items.title: Necesita un dentista
items.text: El dolor de muelas y el absceso dental necesitan un dentista. El antibiótico solo no arregla el diente.

sections.h2: Pez araña (peixe-aranha) — frecuente en las playas portuguesas
paragraphs: El pez araña se esconde en la arena en aguas poco profundas, sobre todo en el Algarve y en la costa oeste. Pisarlo causa un dolor brusco e intenso en el pie.

Primeros auxilios: sumerja el pie en agua tan caliente como tolere sin quemarse (pruébela con la otra mano) durante 30 a 90 minutos. Los socorristas conocen el procedimiento. El paracetamol o el ibuprofeno ayudan. Si en los días siguientes la herida se pone roja, caliente e hinchada, consulte a un médico.
Usar escarpines en la orilla, sobre todo con marea baja, evita la mayoría de las picaduras.

sections.h2: Medusas y carabela portuguesa (caravela-portuguesa)
paragraphs: Salga del agua. Aclare con agua de mar — no con agua dulce — y retire los tentáculos visibles con pinzas o con guantes, sin frotar. Después, el agua templada puede aliviar el dolor.

La picadura de carabela portuguesa es más dolorosa y puede dar síntomas generales. Siga las indicaciones de los socorristas y las banderas de la playa; si hay dolor en el pecho, dificultad para respirar o desmayo, llame al 112.

sections.h2: Quemadura solar y alergia al sol

items.title: Fresco, no frío
items.text: Duchas frescas o paños húmedos, beber mucho, y aftersun o una crema hidratante ligera.

items.title: Para el dolor
items.text: Paracetamol o ibuprofeno de la farmacia, si normalmente puede tomarlos.

items.title: No toque las ampollas
items.text: No las reviente. Cubra las ampollas rotas con un apósito limpio y evite el sol.

items.title: Alergia al sol
items.text: Una erupción con picor y granitos en la piel expuesta en los primeros días de vacaciones suele ser una erupción polimorfa lumínica. La sombra y un antihistamínico de farmacia suelen ayudar; los casos intensos o persistentes se pueden valorar por vídeo.

sections.h2: Mosquitos y garrapatas
paragraphs: Las picaduras de mosquito en Portugal suelen dar solo picor: un antihistamínico en pastillas o crema de farmacia, e intente no rascarse. En Madeira hay mosquitos Aedes — use repelente.

Retire las garrapatas con pinzas finas, cerca de la piel, y anote la fecha. Fiebre, dolor de cabeza o erupción en las dos semanas siguientes requieren un médico: la fiebre botonosa mediterránea existe en Portugal y tiene tratamiento.

faq.q: ¿Puede un médico valorar una erupción por vídeo?
faq.a: A menudo sí — con buena luz y un primer plano. Si la médica necesita explorarle en persona o pedir pruebas, se lo dirá.

faq.q: ¿Me pueden tratar una picadura infectada?
faq.a: Si la médica diagnostica una infección bacteriana de la piel, puede recetar el tratamiento por receta electrónica. Muchas picaduras rojas son solo inflamación y no necesitan antibiótico.

faq.q: ¿Qué pido en la farmacia?
faq.a: Para la quemadura: aftersun o un gel calmante, y analgésicos. Para picaduras con picor: un antihistamínico oral o una crema suave. Informe al farmacéutico de otros medicamentos y de un posible embarazo.

sections.h2: La tracina (peixe-aranha) — frequente sulle spiagge portoghesi
paragraphs: La tracina si nasconde nella sabbia in acqua bassa, soprattutto in Algarve e sulla costa occidentale. Pestarla provoca un dolore improvviso e intenso al piede.

Primo soccorso: immerga il piede in acqua calda quanto riesce a sopportare senza scottarsi (la provi con l’altra mano) per 30–90 minuti. I bagnini conoscono la procedura. Paracetamolo o ibuprofene aiutano. Se nei giorni successivi la ferita diventa rossa, calda e gonfia, consulti un medico.
Le scarpette da scoglio in acqua bassa, soprattutto con la bassa marea, evitano la maggior parte delle punture.

sections.h2: Meduse e caravella portoghese (caravela-portuguesa)
paragraphs: Esca dall’acqua. Sciacqui con acqua di mare — non acqua dolce — e rimuova i filamenti visibili con una pinzetta o con i guanti, senza strofinare. Dopo, l’acqua calda può alleviare il dolore.

La puntura della caravella portoghese è più dolorosa e può dare sintomi generali. Segua i bagnini e le bandiere della spiaggia; in caso di dolore al petto, difficoltà a respirare o svenimento, chiami il 112.

items.text: Un’eruzione pruriginosa a puntini sulla pelle esposta nei primi giorni di vacanza è spesso un’eruzione polimorfa solare. Ombra e un antistaminico della farmacia di solito aiutano; i casi forti o persistenti si possono valutare in video.

sections.h2: Zanzare e zecche
paragraphs: In Portogallo le punture di zanzara di solito danno solo prurito: un antistaminico in compresse o in crema, e cerchi di non grattarsi. A Madeira ci sono zanzare Aedes — usi un repellente.

Rimuova le zecche con una pinzetta sottile, vicino alla pelle, e annoti la data. Febbre, mal di testa o eruzione nelle due settimane successive richiedono un medico: la febbre bottonosa del Mediterraneo esiste in Portogallo e si cura.

faq.a: Se il medico diagnostica un’infezione batterica della pelle, può prescrivere la terapia con ricetta elettronica. Molte punture arrossate sono solo infiammazione e non richiedono antibiotico.

faq.q: Cosa chiedo in farmacia?
faq.a: Per la scottatura: doposole o un gel lenitivo, e un antidolorifico. Per le punture che prudono: un antistaminico orale o una crema leggera. Segnali al farmacista altri farmaci e un’eventuale gravidanza.

sections.h2: SNS, privato o online — cosa fa per lei?

items.title: SNS (sistema pubblico)
items.text: Pensato per i residenti con un medico di famiglia. Da turista, l’accesso pubblico realistico è il pronto soccorso (urgência) — adatto alle vere emergenze, ma con lunghe attese per i problemi non urgenti.

items.title: Clinica o ospedale privato
items.text: Rapidi e spesso con personale che parla inglese a Lisbona, Porto, in Algarve e nelle altre zone turistiche, ma costosi senza assicurazione, e bisogna arrivarci.

items.title: Consulto online (Lon Clinic)
items.text: Ideale per problemi comuni e non urgenti. Un medico iscritto all’Ordem dos Médicos la visita in video. Se serve, la ricetta è elettronica e vale in qualsiasi farmacia del Portogallo. Consulti in inglese, spagnolo o portoghese. 39 €, visibili prima del pagamento.

sections.h2: Servono l’assicurazione viaggio o la TEAM?
paragraphs: I cittadini UE/SEE con la Tessera europea di assicurazione malattia (TEAM) accedono alle cure pubbliche necessarie alle stesse condizioni dei residenti — la tessera non copre i consulti privati od online.
I visitatori extra-UE dovrebbero avere un’assicurazione viaggio. Lon Clinic può rilasciare una ricevuta per il rimborso se la polizza copre le cure ambulatoriali o la telemedicina.
Per un problema rapido e non urgente, un consulto online è spesso più semplice che districarsi tra le pratiche per le cure pubbliche.

sections.h2: E se non parlo inglese?
paragraphs: Non offriamo consulti in italiano. Se l’inglese non le è comodo, lo spagnolo è spesso la scelta più naturale per chi parla italiano. Lo indichi al momento della prenotazione.

faq.q: Un turista può presentarsi in un ospedale portoghese?
faq.a: Sì, per le emergenze — i pronto soccorso pubblici curano tutti, qualunque sia la nazionalità. Ai non residenti può essere addebitato il costo, e non è pensato per i problemi minori.

faq.q: Usare il SNS da turista ha un costo?
faq.a: Ai non residenti senza TEAM né iscrizione portoghese in genere vengono addebitate le cure, comprese le visite al pronto soccorso.

faq.q: Quanto in fretta posso avere un consulto online?
faq.a: Spesso ci sono appuntamenti in giornata, sette giorni su sette. Sceglie l’orario al momento della prenotazione. Il consulto costa 39 €.

faq.q: La ricetta funziona in qualsiasi farmacia?
faq.a: Quando viene rilasciata, è una ricetta elettronica portoghese. La ritira in qualsiasi farmacia del Paese con il codice ricevuto via SMS o email.

sections.h2: La farmacia può aiutarmi senza ricetta?
paragraphs: Le farmacie portoghesi (farmácias) sono ben preparate e possono consigliare prodotti da banco per alleviare i sintomi lievi.
Non possono dare antibiotici. In Portogallo l’antibiotico per la cistite richiede sempre un medico. Se i sintomi sono lievi, il farmacista resta un buon primo passo per capire cosa fare.

faq.q: Posso comprare un antibiotico per la cistite senza ricetta in Portogallo?
faq.a: No. Gli antibiotici richiedono sempre la ricetta, anche per una cistite comune. Il farmacista può aiutare con i sintomi e i passi successivi, non con l’antibiotico.

faq.q: Quanto costa il consulto online?

faq.q: Sono un uomo con questi sintomi. Posso prenotare online?
faq.a: L’infezione urinaria nell’uomo non si tratta come una cistite semplice. Non usi questa pagina come scorciatoia per l’antibiotico. Con febbre o dolore al fianco, pronto soccorso. Altrimenti prenoti un consulto generale e si aspetti una valutazione più attenta, spesso di persona.

howItWorks.title: Qualsiasi farmacia in Portogallo
howItWorks.text: Porti il codice in una farmácia. La maggior parte delle ricette elettroniche si ritira in giornata.

sections.h2: La farmacia può rinnovare direttamente?
paragraphs: In casi limitati — soprattutto farmaci cronici già su una ricetta elettronica portoghese — la farmacia può dare una piccola scorta senza nuova ricetta. Non è garantito e dipende dal farmaco. Non ci conti come piano.

sections.h2: Una ricetta italiana vale in Portogallo?
paragraphs: Una ricetta di un altro Paese UE può in linea di principio essere spedita in Portogallo se contiene i dati richiesti (nome del farmaco o principio attivo, dose, dati del medico e firma). In pratica molte farmacie sono prudenti con le ricette straniere, soprattutto le ricette elettroniche che esistono solo nel sistema italiano.
La TEAM non paga un consulto privato o Lon Clinic. Possiamo rilasciare una ricevuta se la sua assicurazione viaggio copre le cure ambulatoriali o la telemedicina.

faq.q: Posso rinnovare qualsiasi farmaco così?
faq.a: La maggior parte dei farmaci cronici stabili — pressione, tiroide, colesterolo, contraccezione, molti inalatori — si può valutare così. Antibiotici, farmaci GLP-1 per dimagrire, nuovi farmaci psichiatrici o per il sonno e oppioidi non si rinnovano su questo percorso.

faq.q: Quanto è rapida la nuova ricetta?
faq.a: Se il medico la rilascia alla fine della videochiamata, il codice arriva di solito via SMS o email subito o in pochi minuti — non è una promessa che tutto avvenga in meno di un’ora dalla prenotazione.

faq.q: Quanto costa?
faq.a: 19 € da Lon Clinic per il videoconsulto di rinnovo. Se il medico ritiene che sia un problema nuovo, glielo dirà — potrebbe servire un consulto generale completo da 39 €.

faq.q: L’assicurazione viaggio lo copre?
faq.a: Alcune polizze coprono le cure ambulatoriali o la telemedicina. Controlli la sua. Lon Clinic può rilasciare una ricevuta. Molti visitatori pagano semplicemente i 19 €.
